sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and connections
sections.what: Brings in the data fetching tools, the generated server client, the assistant panel, the slide view, the progress track and the run control buttons that the run screen uses.
sections.why: Likely reason: the screen is assembled from shared pieces. Not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The server client names come from a shared package. If those names change, this screen will fail to build.

sections.name: LL_STAGES, RunViewMode
sections.title: Stage labels and view modes
sections.what: Holds the plain-language name, icon and one-sentence purpose for each pipeline stage, and defines the three view modes: all, analysis and output.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets people see what each stage does without reading raw stage names.
sections.watch_out: Stage keys must match the names sent by the server. An unknown key falls back to a converted raw name.

sections.name: LessonsReplay
sections.title: Replay settings contract
sections.what: Describes everything a prepared walkthrough can ask the screen to show: a recipe, a section to scroll to, a fact to open, highlighted facts, a text amendment, an export action, slide edits, recorded assistant replies and playback state.
sections.why: The comment says replay never changes the saved run.
sections.watch_out: All replay fields are optional, so any new field must be handled wherever the screen uses replay.

sections.name: Readable
sections.title: Readable value display
sections.what: Turns saved structured data (lists and nested groups) into readable indented lists with plain key names, instead of raw text. Stops at a nesting depth of four.
sections.why: The comment says raw data is never shown to people.
sections.watch_out: Anything deeper than four levels shows as nested detail instead of its content.

sections.name: StatusPill
sections.title: Run status badge
sections.what: Shows the run's status word in a coloured badge: green-red for success, pale red for failure, gold for insufficient evidence, sand for cancelled or interrupted, and a spinner while running or queued.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick visual sign of run state.
sections.watch_out: Any status not in the list falls back to a grey default, so a new status shows without its colour.

sections.name: Block
sections.title: Titled section wrapper
sections.what: A reusable box with a heading, content and an optional highlight ring. It accepts a reference so the page can scroll to it.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each part of the output looking the same and makes scrolling possible.
sections.watch_out: The scroll targets depend on the reference being passed in.

sections.name: LessonsRunView (part 1)
sections.title: Main run screen setup
sections.what: Receives the run ID, optional mode and replay settings. Sets up scroll anchors, polls the run every 2.5 seconds until it is final, loads the presentation only for finished live runs, and wraps the save and question calls with conflict handling that reloads the latest version.
sections.why: The comment says replay never sends presentation or assistant requests.
sections.watch_out: Polling stops only at a final status, and saves depend on the expected revision matching the server.

sections.name: LessonsRunView (part 2)
sections.title: Recipe preparation and citation opening
sections.what: Applies any replay text amendment to pillars and slides by exact-text replacement, builds a lookup of facts, and opens a citation when a replay asks for one. Defines the fact buttons shown beside content, and shows loading placeholders while data loads.
sections.why: Likely reason: the amendment lets a walkthrough show a changed wording without saving it.
sections.watch_out: The amendment replaces every exact match, including matches in unrelated slides.

sections.name: LessonsRunView: if
sections.title: Error state and actions
sections.what: Shows an error box with retry and start-over buttons if the run cannot be loaded. Otherwise sets up the header flags for each view mode, a retry action for failed runs, and an export action that uses the replay export if one is provided, or downloads the PPTX from the server.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user recover from a load failure without refreshing the whole page.
sections.watch_out: Export errors are shown as text under the header rather than as a pop-up.

sections.name: LessonsRunView (part 4)
sections.title: Header, notices and output actions
sections.what: Shows the page title, status badge, cancel, ledger download, retry, export and new scope buttons. Also shows notices for cancelled or interrupted runs, the saved run details, retry and export errors, the run error text, and a note when the pipeline stopped for insufficient evidence.
sections.why: The notices explain why no lessons deck was produced in those cases.
sections.watch_out: Export only appears when the run has finished and its output is ready. An insufficient evidence run cannot be resumed.

summary: The main screen for one lessons analysis run. It shows progress and status, the saved lessons output, and export and editing controls.
purpose: Let a user follow a run, review its results, ask questions about it and export the deck.
why: Likely reason: one screen covers the whole life of a run, from live progress to finished output. The reason is otherwise not stated in the code.
how: 1. Loads the run and checks its status every 2.5 seconds until it reaches a final state. 2. For finished live runs, loads the saved presentation and wires up saving edits and asking questions, with conflict handling. 3. Builds the recipe to show, applying any replay amendment. 4. Shows an error screen if the run cannot load. 5. Shows the header with status, cancel, ledger, retry, export and new scope buttons, then notices for cancelled, interrupted or insufficient evidence runs, then the output. Sections 11 to 13 were not provided.
inputs: The run ID, optional view mode, optional replay settings, and server responses for the run, presentation, saved edits and questions.
outputs: The run screen. Server calls go out to save edits, ask questions, retry a run and download the PPTX or ledger.
risks: Polling stops only at a final status, so a status that never becomes final keeps the screen checking. Live saves depend on the server's revision check. Replay amendments replace every exact match, which can change more text than intended. Sections 11 to 13 were not provided.
debug: If the screen never settles, check the status values and whether a final state is reached. If export is missing, check that the run succeeded and that its output is ready. If saves report a conflict, reload and check the revision number. If a stage label shows as a raw name, check the stage key list.
